item.title: Chinese study on US missile defense gaps validated by Iran war, analysts say
item.description: As the US-Israeli war on Iran enters its second week, Iran's deployment of hypersonic missiles has exposed vulnerabilities in some of the world's most advanced air defense systems — outcomes that a Chinese research team had predicted in a paper published before the conflict began.

item.title: Mideast war widens as Iran missiles hit Tel Aviv, Gulf states intercept strikes
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced this week that its hypersonic missiles and advanced drones bypassed the US-made THAAD missile defense system and struck targets in central Israel, including the Israeli Defense Ministry building and Ben Gurion International Airport near Tel Aviv, according to the IRGC's statement carried by Iranian state news agency IRNA. The claims, which Israel has disputed, came as a Chinese research paper published days earlier predicted that US missile defenses were "dangerously outmatched" by hypersonic threats — an assessment that footage from the conflict appeared to support.

item.title: Reports: Israel used Blue Sparrow missile to kill Khamenei
item.description: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed on February 28 in a joint U.S.-Israeli airstrike on his compound in Tehran, in what Israel dubbed Operation Roaring Lion. Reports now indicate that among the weapons deployed was the Blue Sparrow, an Israeli air-launched ballistic missile that briefly exits the atmosphere before plunging nearly vertically onto its target at hypersonic speed.

item.title: Oil posts strongest weekly gain since 2022 as Hormuz stays shut
item.description: The week-long U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran has sent global oil and liquefied petroleum gas prices sharply higher, with crude benchmarks posting their strongest weekly gains since 2022 as the Strait of Hormuz — a chokepoint for roughly 20% of the world's oil supply — remains effectively closed to commercial shipping.

item.title: IRGC strikes eighth vessel as Hormuz oil traffic drops to zero
item.description:
The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran has paralyzed one of the world's most critical shipping corridors, halting oil tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and sending shockwaves through global energy markets and supply chains now entering a second week.

As of Wednesday, the number of oil tankers passing through the strait — a narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that normally carries roughly 20 percent of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas — had dropped to zero, down from 37 vessels the day before hostilities began on February 28, according to Reuters. On March 7, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps struck yet another commercial vessel, a Malta-flagged tanker, bringing the total number of ships hit to at least eight.

item.title: Over 200 metabolic enzymes found on human DNA, study reveals
item.description: More than two hundred metabolic enzymes — many of which were thought to operate exclusively in the mitochondria — have been found sitting directly on human DNA inside the cell nucleus, according to a study published March 6 in Nature Communications. The finding reveals that each cell type, tissue, and cancer harbors a distinct "nuclear metabolic fingerprint," opening a new front in understanding how tumors grow and resist treatment.

item.title: Balen Shah's party heads for landslide in Nepal's post-protest election
item.description:
Rapper-turned-politician Balendra Shah's Rastriya Swatantra Party is heading toward a sweeping victory in Nepal's general elections, upending decades of dominance by the country's traditional political establishment. As of Saturday, the RSP had won 20 seats and was leading in 98 others out of 165 directly elected constituencies in the 275-member House of Representatives, according to the latest Election Commission data reported by NDTV.

Shah, 35, delivered the most dramatic result of the election by unseating four-time former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli in his own stronghold of Jhapa-5. According to final results from the constituency, Shah received 68,348 votes to Oli's 18,734 — a margin of 49,614 votes. The RSP also took the lead in all constituencies across the Kathmandu Valley and made deep inroads in other provinces.

item.title: Protests erupt across Havana after days without power
item.description:
Nighttime protests broke out across Havana on Friday, March 6, as Cubans endured what some reported as more than 60 hours without electricity following the collapse of the country's National Electric System earlier in the week. Residents in Centro Habana, Vedado, Marianao, La Habana Vieja, and San Miguel del Padrón banged pots and pans and shouted slogans in the darkness, according to videos circulating on social media.

The demonstrations mark the latest eruption of public anger on an island caught between a crumbling power grid and an intensifying U.S. campaign to cut off its fuel supplies. Analyst Thomas van Linge reported on X that "protests against the communist regime are now being reported in several neighborhoods across the capital" after residents spent more than 60 hours without power. Spain's El Mundo reported that the energy crisis reached one of its worst points on Friday, with roughly 70% of the island left in the dark.

item.title: Turkey weighs deploying F-16 jets to Northern Cyprus
item.description:
Turkey is weighing the deployment of F-16 fighter jets to Northern Cyprus as the fallout from the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran continues to reshape the eastern Mediterranean security landscape.

Turkish Defense Ministry sources confirmed Saturday that "phased planning is underway to ensure the security of the TRNC," adding that "the deployment of F-16 aircraft to the island is among the options being considered," according to Turkey's state-run Anadolu Agency. Reuters separately reported the move is part of a series of measures aimed at safeguarding the self-declared Turkish Cypriot state as tensions rise in the region. Bloomberg also reported that Turkey was considering deploying F-16 warplanes to bolster northern Cypriot defenses.

item.title: UAE president declares 'we are no easy prey' as Iranian strikes enter second week
item.description:
UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan declared his country was "in a period of war" but resilient, delivering his first public remarks since Iran began launching missiles and drones at the Gulf state over a week ago. "The UAE has thick skin and bitter flesh — we are no easy prey," he said during a visit to wounded civilians at Sheikh Shakhbout Medical City in Abu Dhabi on Friday, according to comments broadcast on Abu Dhabi TV on Saturday.

The Emirati leader, who also serves as ruler of Abu Dhabi, praised the role of citizens and the military and pledged to protect everyone living in the federation. "We will carry out our duty towards our country, our people, and our residents who are also part of our family," he said. He spoke with injured individuals and their families from the UAE, Sudan, Iran, Pakistan, and India, reassuring them "they are among their family in the UAE".

item.title: Trump threatens expanded strikes on Iran as war enters second week
item.description:
President Donald Trump warned Saturday that Iran "will be hit very hard" and said the United States is considering striking "areas and groups of people that were not considered for targeting up until this moment in time," a sharp escalation in rhetoric as the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its eighth day with no end in sight.

"Today Iran will be hit very hard!" Trump wrote in a social media post in the early hours of Saturday, adding that attacks would continue "until they surrender or, more likely, completely collapse!" In a separate post, he cited Iran's "bad behavior" as justification for giving "serious consideration for complete destruction and certain death" to previously untargeted areas.

item.title: Dubai airport resumes flights after Iranian drone explodes near terminal
item.description:
Dubai International Airport, the world's busiest hub for international travel, was forced to temporarily halt all flight operations on Saturday morning after an Iranian drone exploded in close proximity to one of its terminal buildings, marking the second time in a week that the airport has come under direct threat from Tehran's retaliatory strikes on Gulf states.

Emirates, the Middle East's largest airline, announced in a post on X that all flights to and from Dubai were suspended until further notice, urging passengers not to travel to the airport. The carrier resumed operations by early afternoon local time, advising only passengers with confirmed bookings to proceed to the airport.

item.title: Guinea dissolves 40 political parties, including top opposition groups
item.description:
Guinea's government dissolved 40 political parties in a late-night decree issued Friday, stripping the country's three main opposition groups of their legal status less than two months after former junta leader Mamady Doumbouya was sworn in as president. The Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralisation, Ibrahima Kalil Condé, ordered the dissolutions for "failure to fulfil their obligations," according to the decree broadcast on state television.

Among the disbanded parties are the Union of Democratic Forces of Guinea (UFDG), led by exiled former prime minister Cellou Dalein Diallo; the Rally of the Guinean People (RPG), the party of ousted former president Alpha Condé; and the Union of Republican Forces (UFR), founded by another exiled former prime minister, Sidya Touré.

item.title: Iran fires 7 missile barrages at Israel as war enters second week
item.description: Iran launched at least seven waves of ballistic missiles targeting central Israel since midnight Saturday, triggering air raid sirens across Tel Aviv, Jerusalem, and surrounding areas as the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran entered its second week with no signs of abating.

item.title: Trump says Cuba negotiating deal at Miami summit
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared Saturday that Cuba is actively negotiating a deal with the United States, making the announcement at the "Shield of the Americas" summit in Miami, where he gathered leaders from across Latin America. Trump said Cuba is "at the end of the line" and that discussions are underway with him and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

"They are looking to negotiate, and they are in talks with Marco, myself, and several others. I believe that a deal could be easily established with Cuba," Trump said at the event held at Trump National Doral. The remarks escalate weeks of mounting pressure on Havana and follow Trump telling CNN on Friday that Cuba "is going to fall pretty soon," adding that he plans to "put Marco over there" to handle the situation.

item.title: Chinese scientists use AI to build first chemical map of moon's far side
item.description:
Chinese scientists have built the first high-precision chemical map of the moon's entire surface, including its long-unmapped far side, by combining artificial intelligence with data from China's historic Chang'e-6 mission, according to a study published in the peer-reviewed journal Nature Sensors.

The research, led by the Shanghai Institute of Technical Physics (SITP) under the Chinese Academy of Sciences in collaboration with Tongji University and other Chinese institutions, used a residual convolutional neural network to analyze spectral imaging data calibrated with ground-truth samples retrieved from the far side. The result is the first global distribution map of major lunar oxides that incorporates actual far-side measurements rather than relying solely on near-side calibration data.

item.title: Iran's hypersonic missiles test US, Israeli defenses as conflict enters second week
item.description: As the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran enters its second week, Iranian hypersonic and maneuverable ballistic missiles have repeatedly penetrated the layered air defense systems deployed across the region, raising urgent questions about the ability of existing Western interceptors to counter next-generation missile threats. A Chinese research paper published the same day the conflict began appears to have predicted those vulnerabilities with striking accuracy.

item.title: Trump doesn't rule out ground troops in Iran
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Saturday declined to rule out sending American ground forces into Iran to secure the country's stockpile of enriched uranium, saying such a move "is something we could consider later" even as the U.S. air campaign enters its second week.

Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One after attending a dignified transfer ceremony at Dover Air Force Base for six fallen soldiers, Trump said ground troops would only be deployed "for a very good reason" but acknowledged the possibility when asked specifically about securing nuclear material believed to be stored in underground tunnels near Isfahan.

"We haven't discussed it," Trump told The Guardian when asked about troops securing enriched uranium. "At some point, perhaps we will. It would be a significant step. Right now we're decimating. We haven't pursued that yet, but it's something we could consider later".

item.title: Iran hits Gulf states hours after president's apology
item.description:
Iran launched a fresh barrage of missiles and drones at Gulf Arab states on Saturday, striking targets across the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar — just hours after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian issued a televised apology to neighboring countries and pledged to halt attacks on them unless Iran was attacked from their territory.

The contradiction between Pezeshkian's words and the continued strikes underscored deep rifts within Iran's leadership as the war with the United States and Israel entered its second week.

item.title: Trump formally recognizes Venezuela's Rodriguez government
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced Saturday that the United States has "formally" and "legally" recognized the Venezuelan government led by acting President Delcy Rodríguez, deepening a relationship born from the U.S. military operation that ousted Nicolás Maduro in January.

Speaking at the Shield of the Americas Summit in Doral, Florida, Trump said the administration has "been working closely with the new president of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez," adding that "she's doing a great job working with us." He also touted a new agreement allowing the sale of Venezuelan gold and minerals to American buyers, calling it "a historic gold deal with Venezuela."
